html:
The Tübatulabal are an Indigenous people of the Kern River valley in the southern Sierra Nevada of California, including land now in Sequoia National Park. Their language forms its own branch of the Uto-Aztecan family.

They lived in small villages and moved with the seasons, gathering acorns and pine nuts, hunting deer and fishing the Kern River. They traded with the Yokuts in the valley below, and lived beside the Kawaiisu to the south and the Western Mono to the north.

Gold was found on the Kern River in the 1850s, a few years into the California Gold Rush. Miners and ranchers moved in, and in 1863 soldiers killed dozens of Native men at Keysville. Many survivors then worked on ranches. The Tübatulabal, now a few hundred people, still live in the Kern valley.
